title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — 9.3.1 Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Adverbs)

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Adverbs add information to verbs. In this sub-strand you will tell adverbs of manner, time and place apart, and you will use them in speech and writing. Manner answers how, time answers when, and place answers where. The sentences use a health theme and stay respectful of people living with HIV.

## Strand 9.0: HIV and AIDS
Sub-strand 9.3.1: Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Adverbs)
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) distinguish adverbs of manner, time and place for effective communication
b) use adverbs of manner, time and place correctly in both oral and written sentences
c) realise the importance of adverbs in oral and written communication

## What this sub-strand covers
• Adverbs of time
• Adverbs of place
• Adverbs of manner

## Key inquiry questions
1. Where do you live?
2. How do you do your work?
3. When do we come to school?

## Core competencies
• Communication and Collaboration: This is manifested when the learner play games involving categorising different types of adverbs collaboratively.
• Self-efficacy: This is gained when learner constructs sentences using adverbs for daily communication.

## Values
• Integrity: This is nurtured when the learner displays honesty as they create a list of adverbs and construct sentences individually.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• HIV and AIDS Education, Communicable and Non-communicable Diseases: These issues are enhanced as the learner interacts with the theme in various activities and makes sentences with adverbs that are derived from the theme of HIV and AIDS.

## Links to other learning areas
• The learner applies the knowledge gained from studying adverbs to their learning of word classes in Kiswahili.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 English Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Theme 9.0 HIV and AIDS, Sub-strand 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Adverbs of manner

LESSON 1: ADVERBS OF MANNER
===========================

## What you will learn
• Recognise an adverb of manner as a word that tells how an action is done.
• Use common adverbs of manner in sentences.
• Notice that not every adverb of manner ends in -ly.

Curriculum outcomes: a) distinguish adverbs of manner, time and place for effective communication; b) use adverbs of manner, time and place correctly in both oral and written sentences

## Introduction
The nurse spoke is a thin sentence. The nurse spoke kindly tells us the manner of the speaking. That one word changes what we picture and how we are asked to treat people.

## Notes
### What an adverb of manner does
An **adverb of manner** tells us how an action is done. It answers the question How?

- The nurse spoke **kindly**.
- We listened **carefully**.
- He closed the packet **gently**.
- She explained the chart **clearly**.

Many of these words are made by adding -ly to an adjective: kind becomes kindly, careful becomes carefully, safe becomes safely. If the adjective ends in y, change y to i before -ly: easy becomes easily, happy becomes happily.

### Manner without -ly
Some very common adverbs of manner do not end in -ly.

- She sings **well**.
- They worked **hard**.
- He ran **fast**.

Well, not goodly, is the adverb that matches the adjective good. He plays well. Hard and fast can also be adjectives, so test them with How? How did they work? Hard. Then hard is an adverb of manner in that sentence.

### Where to put the adverb
An adverb of manner often comes just after the verb, or after the object.

- She listened carefully.
- She read the chart carefully.

Do not break a verb from its object with the adverb if the sentence becomes clumsy. Prefer She closed the gate carefully, not She closed carefully the gate.

### Manner in this theme
How we speak about health matters as much as the facts. We ask questions politely. We correct a mistake calmly. We welcome a classmate warmly. None of those adverbs changes the science. They stop the science from being used as an insult.

People living with HIV should be treated fairly. Fairly is an adverb of manner. It answers How should they be treated?

### A short rhyme
The nurse spoke kindly, the class listened well,
She showed us the chart and the facts she could tell.
We washed our hands gently and put blades away,
How we treat people matters the whole of the day.

Kindly, well and gently are adverbs of manner. Find them before you worry about the rhythm.

## Key words
• adverb — a word that tells us more about a verb, such as how, when or where an action happens
• adverb of manner — an adverb that answers How?, such as kindly or carefully
• fairly — in a just and respectful way

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Which word is the adverb of manner in: The boys whispered unkindly?

Working:
1. Ask How did they whisper?
2. The word that answers is unkindly.

Answer: unkindly

### Example 2
Make an adverb of manner from careful and use it with washed.

Working:
1. Add -ly to careful.
2. Put the adverb after the verb or the object.

Answer: We washed our hands carefully.

## Activity: How did they do it?
You will need: Adverb cards: kindly, carefully, clearly, gently, safely, well, fast, calmly, Verb cards: spoke, listened, washed, ran, explained
1. Spread the cards face up.
2. In groups, match a verb card to an adverb card and say a full sentence about health or friendship.
3. Ask How? after each sentence to prove the word is an adverb of manner.
4. Recite the rhyme and raise a hand when you hear an adverb of manner.

## Practice
1. What question does an adverb of manner answer?
2. Write the adverb made from easy.
3. Choose the adverb of manner: She explained the facts clearly.
4. Write a sentence using well to tell how a person sings or works.

## Summary
• An adverb of manner answers How?
• Many are made with -ly, but well, hard and fast are common exceptions.
• Place the adverb so the sentence still sounds natural.

### Answers to practice
1. How?
2. easily
3. clearly
4. Any correct sentence, for example: She sings well.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Adverbs of time and place

LESSON 2: ADVERBS OF TIME AND PLACE
===================================

## What you will learn
• Recognise adverbs of time and adverbs of place.
• Use them to say when and where an action happens.
• Sort adverbs into manner, time and place.

Curriculum outcomes: a) distinguish adverbs of manner, time and place for effective communication; b) use adverbs of manner, time and place correctly in both oral and written sentences

## Introduction
Where do you live? When do we come to school? Those two questions need different kinds of answer. One answer is a place. The other is a time. Adverbs can give both.

## Notes
### Adverbs of time
An **adverb of time** tells us when an action happens. It answers When?

- We learnt the facts **today**.
- She visited the clinic **yesterday**.
- He takes his medicine **every day**.
- Come **early**.
- We will talk **soon**.
- I have **already** washed my hands.
- They **never** share a razor blade.

Every day is two words working as one adverb of time. Already, always, never, now, soon, early, today and yesterday are others you will meet often. Early does not end in -ly, but it still answers When? in Come early.

Time adverbs can stand at the end of the sentence or at the beginning. Today we wrote a promise. We wrote a promise today. Both are correct. A time word at the beginning is followed by the rest of the sentence, and the first word still takes a capital letter.

### Adverbs of place
An **adverb of place** tells us where an action happens. It answers Where?

- Sit **here**.
- The chart is **there**.
- Please come **inside**.
- We play **outside**.
- Keep the blades **inside**.
- The clinic is **nearby**.

Here, there, inside, outside, everywhere and nearby are adverbs of place. A short phrase can do the same job: at school, at the clinic, at home. For this lesson you may treat those phrases as place expressions that answer Where?

### Do not mix the three questions
Ask the question before you name the adverb.

- How did she speak? Kindly. Manner.
- When did she speak? Today. Time.
- Where did she speak? Here. Place.

She spoke kindly here today uses all three, in a common order: manner, then place, then time. You do not have to use all three at once. One accurate adverb is better than three that do not fit.

### Sentences that stay accurate
He takes his medicine every day. Every day is time, and the sentence does not say the medicine is a cure.
Do not leave a used needle here. Here is place, and the instruction is about safety.
We welcomed Amina warmly at school yesterday. Warmly is manner, at school is place, and yesterday is time.

Sorting words into three labelled boxes, or three columns in your book, makes the difference visible.

## Key words
• adverb of time — an adverb that answers When?, such as today, early or every day
• adverb of place — an adverb that answers Where?, such as here, inside or nearby

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Label the adverb in each sentence: We arrived early. The nurse is inside.

Working:
1. Early answers When?, so it is time.
2. Inside answers Where?, so it is place.

Answer: early is an adverb of time; inside is an adverb of place.

### Example 2
Add a place adverb to: Please put the tweezers ________.

Working:
1. The sentence needs Where?
2. Inside or here both fit a safety instruction.

Answer: Please put the tweezers inside. (or here)

## Activity: Three boxes
You will need: Three boxes or columns labelled Manner, Time and Place, Word cards: kindly, today, here, carefully, yesterday, outside, well, soon, nearby, every day, gently, early
1. Play a sorting game. One learner reads a card. The group asks How?, When? or Where? and drops the card in the right box.
2. When the sort is finished, write one sentence for each box about staying healthy or treating people fairly.
3. Recite: We listened carefully here today. Name the manner, place and time words.
4. Swap a sentence with another group and check the labels.

## Practice
1. Is every day an adverb of time or an adverb of place?
2. Choose the adverb of place: Please wait outside.
3. Write a sentence with yesterday about a visit to a clinic.
4. In We listened carefully here today, which word is the adverb of manner?

## Summary
• Adverbs of time answer When? Adverbs of place answer Where?
• A time word can open the sentence or close it.
• Ask How?, When? and Where? before you sort an adverb.

### Answers to practice
1. An adverb of time
2. outside
3. Any correct sentence, for example: We visited the clinic yesterday.
4. carefully

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Using adverbs in speech and writing

LESSON 3: USING ADVERBS IN SPEECH AND WRITING
=============================================

## What you will learn
• Build sentences that use manner, time and place correctly.
• Find adverbs in a short oral story.
• Explain why adverbs make instructions and stories clearer.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use adverbs of manner, time and place correctly in both oral and written sentences; c) realise the importance of adverbs in oral and written communication

## Introduction
Put the blade is not yet a safe instruction. Put the blade inside, carefully, now tells the listener how, where and when. Adverbs earn their place when they make an action clear.

## Notes
### From a list to a sentence
A list of adverbs is only a store. Communication starts when the adverb joins a verb.

- Manner: The class listened quietly.
- Time: The class listened yesterday.
- Place: The class listened outside.
- All three: Yesterday the class listened quietly outside.

Read the last sentence once and test each adverb. Quietly answers How? Outside answers Where? Yesterday answers When? If a word fails its question, it is in the wrong group. School answers neither How? nor When? by itself. At school answers Where?

### A story to hear
Listen for the adverbs as the story is read.

Yesterday, Sister Wairimu spoke calmly here in our room. She never laughed at a question. A boy looked down shyly, then asked his question clearly. After the talk we put the poster up nearby. Today we will greet new learners warmly at the gate. People who take medicine every day can still play happily outside.

Calmly, shyly, clearly, warmly and happily are manner. Yesterday, never, today and every day are time. Here, nearby and outside are place. Happily does not mean that illness is a joke. It means play can still be joyful.

### Why adverbs matter
Without adverbs, warnings and welcome are vague. Come could mean come now or come next week, here or to the office. Take the medicine does not say how often. Every day makes the instruction useful. Kindly stops a correction from sounding like an attack.

Adverbs also make writing honest. If you did the action yesterday, do not write today because it sounds better. Integrity is telling the time and the place as they were.

When you type, you can keep three short lists, one for manner, one for time and one for place, and drag a word into a sentence. Whether you write on paper or on a screen, read the sentence aloud and ask the three questions before you keep it.

## Key words
• instruction — a sentence that tells someone what to do
• vague — unclear, because an important detail is missing

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Improve the instruction by adding time and place: Wash your hands.

Working:
1. When? Now, or before you eat.
2. Where? Here, or at the tap.

Answer: Wash your hands here now. (or Wash your hands at the tap before you eat.)

### Example 2
In the story, is never an adverb of time or of manner?

Working:
1. Ask When does she laugh at a question?
2. Never answers that question. It does not tell how she laughed.

Answer: An adverb of time

## Activity: Listen, list, write
You will need: The short story about Sister Wairimu, Paper or a word processor with a teacher nearby
1. The teacher reads the story twice. On the second reading, write every adverb you hear.
2. Group the words under Manner, Time and Place.
3. Each learner writes three sentences about health or friendship: one with an adverb of manner, one of time and one of place.
4. Read one sentence aloud. The class must say which question it answers: How?, When? or Where?

## Practice
1. Add an adverb of manner to: We greeted the new learner.
2. Which question does every day answer in He takes his medicine every day?
3. Why is Put the blade inside clearer than Put the blade?
4. Write one sentence that uses kindly and today.

## Summary
• An adverb becomes useful when it joins a verb in a real sentence.
• Test manner with How?, time with When? and place with Where?
• Clear adverbs make instructions, stories and welcome more exact.

### Answers to practice
1. Any correct sentence, for example: We greeted the new learner warmly.
2. When?
3. Inside tells where to put it, so the listener knows what to do.
4. Any correct sentence, for example: She spoke kindly today.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 9.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASSES (ADVERBS)
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. An adverb of manner answers ________.
   A. How?
   B. When?
   C. Where?
   D. Who?

2. Which word is an adverb of manner?
   A. yesterday
   B. kindly
   C. here
   D. Monday

3. Which adverb of manner does not end in -ly?
   A. carefully
   B. gently
   C. well
   D. kindly

4. Every day is an adverb of ________.
   A. manner
   B. time
   C. place
   D. noun

5. Which word is an adverb of place?
   A. soon
   B. outside
   C. clearly
   D. always

6. Choose the best sentence.
   A. She closed carefully the packet.
   B. She closed the packet carefully.
   C. Carefully she packet closed.
   D. She careful closed the packet.

7. In We listened quietly here today, which word shows place?
   A. listened
   B. quietly
   C. here
   D. today

8. Complete with an adverb of time: He takes his medicine ________.

9. Why do instructions need adverbs?

10. Write a sentence using an adverb of manner about welcoming a classmate.
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 9.3.1 GRAMMAR IN USE: WORD CLASSES (ADVERBS)
========================================

1. A. How?
   Manner tells how an action is done.

2. B. kindly
   Kindly tells how. Yesterday and Monday tell when. Here tells where.

3. C. well
   Well is the adverb that matches good. It does not take -ly.

4. B. time
   Every day answers When?

5. B. outside
   Outside answers Where? Soon and always answer When? Clearly answers How?

6. B. She closed the packet carefully.
   The adverb of manner fits naturally after the object.

7. C. here
   Here answers Where? Quietly answers How? Today answers When?

8. Any suitable adverb of time, for example every day, today or now.
   The gap answers When?, so it needs an adverb of time.

9. Adverbs tell how, when or where to do the action, so the listener is not left guessing.
   A vague instruction is harder to follow safely.

10. Any correct sentence, for example: We welcomed our classmate warmly.
   Warmly, kindly or politely would show how the welcome was given.

[/DIAGRAM]

## Key words
• adverb of time — an adverb that answers When?, such as today, early or every day
• adverb of place — an adverb that answers Where?, such as here, inside or nearby

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Label the adverb in each sentence: We arrived early. The nurse is inside.

Working:
1. Early answers When?, so it is time.
2. Inside answers Where?, so it is place.

Answer: early is an adverb of time; inside is an adverb of place.

### Example 2
Add a place adverb to: Please put the tweezers ________.

Working:
1. The sentence needs Where?
2. Inside or here both fit a safety instruction.

Answer: Please put the tweezers inside. (or here)

## Activity: Three boxes
You will need: Three boxes or columns labelled Manner, Time and Place, Word cards: kindly, today, here, carefully, yesterday, outside, well, soon, nearby, every day, gently, early
1. Play a sorting game. One learner reads a card. The group asks How?, When? or Where? and drops the card in the right box.
2. When the sort is finished, write one sentence for each box about staying healthy or treating people fairly.
3. Recite: We listened carefully here today. Name the manner, place and time words.
4. Swap a sentence with another group and check the labels.

## Practice
1. Is every day an adverb of time or an adverb of place?
2. Choose the adverb of place: Please wait outside.
3. Write a sentence with yesterday about a visit to a clinic.
4. In We listened carefully here today, which word is the adverb of manner?

## Summary
• Adverbs of time answer When? Adverbs of place answer Where?
• A time word can open the sentence or close it.
• Ask How?, When? and Where? before you sort an adverb.

### Answers to practice
1. An adverb of time
2. outside
3. Any correct sentence, for example: We visited the clinic yesterday.
4. carefully

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using adverbs in speech and writing
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: USING ADVERBS IN SPEECH AND WRITING
=============================================

## What you will learn
• Build sentences that use manner, time and place correctly.
• Find adverbs in a short oral story.
• Explain why adverbs make instructions and stories clearer.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use adverbs of manner, time and place correctly in both oral and written sentences; c) realise the importance of adverbs in oral and written communication

## Introduction
Put the blade is not yet a safe instruction. Put the blade inside, carefully, now tells the listener how, where and when. Adverbs earn their place when they make an action clear.

## Notes
### From a list to a sentence
A list of adverbs is only a store. Communication starts when the adverb joins a verb.

- Manner: The class listened quietly.
- Time: The class listened yesterday.
- Place: The class listened outside.
- All three: Yesterday the class listened quietly outside.

Read the last sentence once and test each adverb. Quietly answers How? Outside answers Where? Yesterday answers When? If a word fails its question, it is in the wrong group. School answers neither How? nor When? by itself. At school answers Where?

### A story to hear
Listen for the adverbs as the story is read.

Yesterday, Sister Wairimu spoke calmly here in our room. She never laughed at a question. A boy looked down shyly, then asked his question clearly. After the talk we put the poster up nearby. Today we will greet new learners warmly at the gate. People who take medicine every day can still play happily outside.

Calmly, shyly, clearly, warmly and happily are manner. Yesterday, never, today and every day are time. Here, nearby and outside are place. Happily does not mean that illness is a joke. It means play can still be joyful.

### Why adverbs matter
Without adverbs, warnings and welcome are vague. Come could mean come now or come next week, here or to the office. Take the medicine does not say how often. Every day makes the instruction useful. Kindly stops a correction from sounding like an attack.

Adverbs also make writing honest. If you did the action yesterday, do not write today because it sounds better. Integrity is telling the time and the place as they were.

When you type, you can keep three short lists, one for manner, one for time and one for place, and drag a word into a sentence. Whether you write on paper or on a screen, read the sentence aloud and ask the three questions before you keep it.

## Key words
• instruction — a sentence that tells someone what to do
• vague — unclear, because an important detail is missing

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Improve the instruction by adding time and place: Wash your hands.

Working:
1. When? Now, or before you eat.
2. Where? Here, or at the tap.

Answer: Wash your hands here now. (or Wash your hands at the tap before you eat.)

### Example 2
In the story, is never an adverb of time or of manner?

Working:
1. Ask When does she laugh at a question?
2. Never answers that question. It does not tell how she laughed.

Answer: An adverb of time

## Activity: Listen, list, write
You will need: The short story about Sister Wairimu, Paper or a word processor with a teacher nearby
1. The teacher reads the story twice. On the second reading, write every adverb you hear.
2. Group the words under Manner, Time and Place.
3. Each learner writes three sentences about health or friendship: one with an adverb of manner, one of time and one of place.
4. Read one sentence aloud. The class must say which question it answers: How?, When? or Where?

## Practice
1. Add an adverb of manner to: We greeted the new learner.
2. Which question does every day answer in He takes his medicine every day?
3. Why is Put the blade inside clearer than Put the blade?
4. Write one sentence that uses kindly and today.

## Summary
• An adverb becomes useful when it joins a verb in a real sentence.
• Test manner with How?, time with When? and place with Where?
• Clear adverbs make instructions, stories and welcome more exact.

### Answers to practice
1. Any correct sentence, for example: We greeted the new learner warmly.
2. When?
3. Inside tells where to put it, so the listener knows what to do.
4. Any correct sentence, for example: She spoke kindly today.

questions.question: An adverb of manner answers ________.
questions.explanation: Manner tells how an action is done.

questions.question: Which word is an adverb of manner?
questions.explanation: Kindly tells how. Yesterday and Monday tell when. Here tells where.

questions.question: Which adverb of manner does not end in -ly?
questions.explanation: Well is the adverb that matches good. It does not take -ly.

questions.question: Every day is an adverb of ________.
Which word is an adverb of place?
questions.explanation: Outside answers Where? Soon and always answer When? Clearly answers How?

questions.question: Choose the best sentence.
questions.explanation: The adverb of manner fits naturally after the object.

questions.question: In We listened quietly here today, which word shows place?
questions.explanation: Here answers Where? Quietly answers How? Today answers When?

questions.question: Complete with an adverb of time: He takes his medicine ________.
questions.answer: Any suitable adverb of time, for example every day, today or now.
questions.explanation: The gap answers When?, so it needs an adverb of time.

questions.question: Why do instructions need adverbs?
questions.answer: Adverbs tell how, when or where to do the action, so the listener is not left guessing.
questions.explanation: A vague instruction is harder to follow safely.

questions.question: Write a sentence using an adverb of manner about welcoming a classmate.
questions.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: We welcomed our classmate warmly.
questions.explanation: Warmly, kindly or politely would show how the welcome was given.
